CO 2 CAPTURE RATES ABOVE 95 PERCENT Commercial-scale demonstration of solvent-based post-combustion CO capture systems at 2 power generation facilities (specifically PC plants) has shown the ability to capture 90 percent of the CO in the flue gas stream. [11] [12] Moreover, field-testing of post-combustion CO capture 2 2 technology as well as vendor and industry feedback on projects currently in the planning stages (including FEED projects sponsored by DOE) indicates that capture rates as high as 95 percent are feasible for both coal- and natural gas-fueled electricity generating units. [13] [14] [15] [16] Given the breadth of publicly-available information supporting the capability for post- combustion capture systems to remove greater than 90 percent of the CO in the treated 2 stream, cases for 90 percent and 95 percent capture on NGCC and PC are presented in the main body of this report. It should be emphasized that technology suppliers (as reflected in vendor-supplied information provided to DOE for this study that included cost and performance estimates for >95 percent CCS (97 percent for NGCC and 99 percent for PC) study cases) as well as subject matter experts acknowledge and support that solvent-based post-combustion CO capture technologies are 2 capable of achieving CO removal rates beyond 95 percent on low-purity streams representative 2 of fossil-fueled combustion. Although technoeconomic analyses of deep decarbonization (≥ 99 percent) of combustion flue gas have been published by others, [17] [18] the relatively limited experience with design and operation of capture systems that can routinely, reliably, and economically achieve very high removal rates requires further study. Technoeconomic analysis of the higher capture rates (97% NGCC and 99% PC) are included in the Appendices to this report. The performance and environmental profile summaries for PC and NGCC cases with CO 2 capture rates greater than 95 percent are shown in Exhibit ES-14; the primary conclusions that can be drawn are:  The emissions of Hg, HCl, PM, NOx, and SO are all at or below the applicable federal 2 regulatory limits currently in effect for PC and NGCC technologies (natural gas contains no Hg or chloride).  For the PC cases, adding a CO capture system with a 99 percent removal rate results in a 2 9 percentage point (24 percent) reduction in efficiency, compared to the non-capture PC cases.
